1	# AGENTS.md — how to work in this repository
2	
3	You are acting as the **detailing engineer** for an architecture practice. The
4	architect owns the design (the IFC model). You own everything *derived* from it:
5	schedules, compliance checks, 2D drawings, and the generator code that produces
6	them. You never edit the design and you never hand-edit generated files — you
7	change the generator and regenerate.
8	
9	## What this repo is
10	
11	An **architecture-as-code harness**. An IFC model goes in; a detailing package
12	comes out, all produced by code in `recognition/`:
13	
14	| Output | Where | Produced by |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| Room / door / window schedules (CSV + MD) | `<out>/schedules/` | `recognition/schedules.py` |
17	| Compliance report (JSON + MD) | `<out>/report.*` | `recognition/rules.py` + `rules/*.yaml` |
18	| Floor-plan sheets (SVG/PDF/PNG/DXF) | `<out>/sheets/` | `recognition/drawings.py` |
19	| Enriched IFC (tags + findings as psets) | `<out>/model.detailed.ifc` | `recognition/cli.py` |
20	| Machine-readable summary | `<out>/summary.json` | `recognition/cli.py` |
21	
22	`examples/<model>/` is the committed output for the two core sample models in
23	`samples/`. It must always match what the current code generates. Larger
24	models under `samples/extended/` (terraced houses, office building) are for
25	manual checks and demos; they are not covered by tests or `examples/` —
26	run them when a change touches geometry, categorisation or drawing layout.
27	
28	## Commands
29	
30	```bash
31	uv sync                                                   # install (Python 3.12, deps in pyproject.toml)
32	uv run pytest -q                                          # the verifier — must be green before any PR
33	uv run recognition run samples/AC20-FZK-Haus.ifc out/fzk  # full package for one model
34	uv run recognition check samples/Duplex.ifc               # compliance only; exit 1 on errors
35	```
36	
37	Regenerate the committed examples after *any* change to `recognition/` or `rules/`:
38	
39	```bash
40	for m in AC20-FZK-Haus Duplex; do uv run recognition run samples/$m.ifc examples/$m --project $m; done
41	```
42	
43	## Procedure for every task
44	
45	1. **Reproduce first.** Run the pipeline on both sample models and look at the
46	   PNG sheets and `report.md` before changing anything. Use the browser or an
47	   image viewer — you are expected to *look at the drawings*.
48	2. **Change the generator, not the output.** Thresholds go in `rules/*.yaml`;
49	   drawing conventions in `drawings.SHEET` / `drawings.STYLE`; new rules are a
50	   YAML entry plus a `@rule("ID")` function in `rules.py`.
51	3. **Regenerate `examples/`** and inspect the diff. Generated files are
52	   deterministic — an unexpected diff in a sheet you did not intend to touch is
53	   a bug.
54	4. **Run `uv run pytest -q`.** Add or update tests when behaviour changes.
55	5. **Open a PR** whose description contains: what changed and why, the
56	   before/after sheet PNGs (attach or link `examples/**/sheets/*.png`), the
57	   compliance status line from `summary.json` for both models, and any
58	   assumption you made about the architecture domain.
59	
60	## Conventions
61	
62	- Units: metres internally; drawings annotate in millimetres without unit
63	  (`3 625`), as architects expect.
64	- Tags `R-nn` / `D-nn` / `W-nn` are assigned by storey then position. They are
65	  identifiers on drawings — do not change the assignment scheme casually; if you
66	  must, say so in the PR because it renumbers every sheet.
67	- DXF layers follow AIA naming (`A-WALL`, `A-DOOR`, `A-GLAZ`, `A-ANNO-DIMS`…).
68	- Sheets are A3 landscape, scale chosen automatically from `SHEET["scales"]`.
69	- Rule values in `rules/residential.yaml` are **demo values**. When a task gives
70	  you a jurisdiction or a source, cite it in the YAML comment next to the value.
71	- Room categories are inferred from names (`model.ROOM_CATEGORIES`, EN + DE).
72	  When a model uses other naming, extend the keyword list rather than special-casing.
73	
74	## Definition of done
75	
76	- `uv run pytest -q` green.
77	- `examples/` regenerated and committed; diff reviewed and explained.
78	- PR description includes sheet images and compliance status for both models.
79	- No generated file was edited by hand.
80	
81	## Forbidden
82	
83	- Editing anything under `samples/` — those are the architect's models.
84	- Hand-editing files under `examples/` or any generated SVG/DXF/PDF/IFC.
85	- Hard-coding thresholds in Python instead of `rules/*.yaml`.
86	- Committing `out/`.
87	- Claiming compliance you did not compute. If a rule cannot be evaluated
88	  (missing data in the model), report it as *not evaluated*, never as pass.
89	
90	## When unsure
91	
92	State the assumption in the PR and proceed with the conservative choice
93	(stricter limit, more information on the drawing). Ask the user only when two
94	readings lead to materially different drawings.
95

It fills in a structured 5 > plan; deterministic code turns that plan into a building, and a deterministic rule 6 > engine judges the result. 7 8 Interactive version (diagrams, full tables): **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7966e4e4-48d4-4909-b472-edaf00fd1b18** 9 10 | | | 11 |---|---| 12 | Geometry source of truth | IFC4 via IfcOpenShell | 13 | Compute | GitHub Actions (secrets stay server-side) | 14 | UI | Static, GitHub Pages, client-side IFC viewer | 15 | Jurisdiction (v1) | Bayern — BayBO Art. 45/46/48 + DIN 18040-2 | 16 | v1 input | Natural language → 2D + 3D. Sketch → 3D is phase 8. | 17 18 Related: [autonomy.md](autonomy.md) · [studio.md](studio.md) · [contracts.md](contracts.md) · [regulations.md](regulations.md) · [adr/](adr/) 19 20 > **Autonomy note.** The interview in L1 below is described as interactive. It is not: 21 > it runs *before* the trigger and produces a sealed brief, after which the run reaches 22 > merged artifacts with nobody in the middle and no approval step. See 23 > [autonomy.md](autonomy.md), which supersedes L1's position. 24 25 --- 26 27 ## 1. The five sources of truth 28 29 Everything else in the repository is *derived* and may be deleted and regenerated. 30 **Nothing derived is ever hand-edited** — not by a human, not by Devin. 31 32 | # | Authority over | Artifact | Written by | Hard rule | 33 |---|---|---|---|---| 34 | SoT-1 | **Intent** | `briefs/.json` | Interview agent, confirmed by user | Never silently inferred; unconfirmed values become recorded `assumptions[]` | 35 | SoT-2 | **Regulation** | `rules/by/*.yaml` | A human curator, with citation | No LLM may author, edit or extend a rule | 36 | SoT-3 | **Geometry** | `design/.py` | The deterministic translator | The only editable geometry artifact | 37 | SoT-4 | **Exchange** | `out/model.ifc` | IfcOpenShell, from SoT-3 | Pure output; regenerated every run | 38 | SoT-5 | **Provenance** | git history + Entire checkpoints | git hooks | Append-only | 39 40 Why the Python DSL and not the IFC is the geometry truth: an IFC diff is unreadable and an 41 agent editing IFC directly can produce a file that parses but is architecturally nonsense. 42 The DSL is ~40 readable lines for a six-room house, every number is a dimension in metres, 43 and a diff shows exactly what moved. That reviewability *is* the safety mechanism. 44 See [ADR-0001](adr/0001-geometry-source-of-truth.md). 45 46 --- 47 48 ## 2. Layers 49 50 Numbering is a real dependency order: L*n* may only read artifacts produced by L*.json` (SoT-1), `questions[]`, `assumptions[]` 70 - **libraries** pydantic, Devin API 71 - **fails when** a returned value falls outside the slot enum/range → rejected and re-asked, never coerced 72 73 ### L2 — Plan synthesis, the architect · *LLM, strongest, temp 0* 74 75 `DesignBrief` in, `ArchitectPlan` out: storeys, rooms with target areas and categories, an 76 adjacency graph, a circulation spine, opening intents. **No coordinates** — the architect 77 reasons in relationships and areas; metres are L3's job. 78 79 Architectural knowledge lives here as retrievable skill files, not model memory: room-size 80 *Richtwerte*, adjacency conventions (bath reached from the hall, not through a bedroom), 81 daylight orientation, circulation width, structural span limits. 82 83 The plan is **pre-checked before geometry exists** — target areas are tested against the 84 ruleset immediately, so "bedroom 6 m² but you asked for barrier-free" costs one cheap call 85 instead of a full geometry round-trip. 86 87 - **reads** `DesignBrief` only — never the chat transcript 88 - **emits** `plans/

.json`, `rationale.md` 89 - **libraries** pydantic, networkx 90 - **fails when** adjacency graph disconnected or areas exceed the footprint → returned with the specific violation 91 92 ### L3 — Deterministic translation · *0 tokens, pure code* 93 94 The heart of the anti-hallucination design, proven by 95 [Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD](https://github.com/Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD) (MIT): a plain 96 Python function turns the typed plan into DSL source at zero token cost. 97 98 `recognition/translate.py` runs rectangular floor-packing over the adjacency graph, derives 99 wall centre-lines from room boundaries, snaps to a 5 cm grid, and places openings where the 100 plan asked. Constructs it cannot express emit a `# TODO_AGENT:` marker with the plan 101 fragment attached — **only those markers are ever sent to a model.** 102 103 - **emits** `design/

.py` (SoT-3) 104 - **libraries** shapely, networkx, rectpack, black (so diffs stay clean) 105 - **fails when** packing cannot satisfy the adjacency graph → infeasibility report back to L2, never a broken plan 106 107 See [ADR-0002](adr/0002-deterministic-translator.md). 108 109 ### L4 — Geometry kernel & artifacts · *no model* 110 111 Executing the DSL builds real IFC4: `IfcWall` with extruded solids, `IfcSpace` carrying 112 name/category/area, `IfcDoor`/`IfcWindow` cut through proper `IfcOpeningElement`s. 113 Semantics matter — a compliance engine must ask "what is the net floor area of this 114 bedroom", which a mesh cannot answer. Everything else is a serializer off that one IFC. 115 116 - **emits** `model.ifc`, `sheets/*.{svg,pdf,png,dxf}`, `model.glb`, `schedules/*.csv` 117 - **libraries** ifcopenshell, shapely, svgwrite, cairosvg, ezdxf, IfcConvert 118 - **fails when** solids self-intersect or an opening misses its wall → assertion, non-zero exit 119 120 ### L5 — Verification, the arbiter · *the gate* 121 122 Four independent deterministic checks. Devin's work is finished when this layer is green, 123 not when Devin says so. 124 125 1. **Regulation** — `recognition/rules.py` emits one result per element checked, pass *or* 126 fail, so coverage is visible alongside violations. 127 2. **Data completeness** — `ifctester` validates against a buildingSMART **IDS** file: 128 are the properties a checker needs actually present? Guidance-tier failures inform, never block. 136 137 ### L6 — Iteration, options & edit · *LLM, router* 138 139 "Make the Schlafzimmer at least 25 m²" is ambiguous by design. A small classifier routes 140 the request to the **lowest layer that can satisfy it**; it re-enters there, never at the top. 141 142 | Request kind | Example | Re-enters at | Cost | 143 |---|---|---|---| 144 | Rule change | "bedrooms must be ≥ 25 m² under the new code" | L0 — edit YAML, re-run L5 | seconds, no model | 145 | Design change | "make the Schlafzimmer at least 25 m²" | L2 — amend plan, re-translate | one strong call | 146 | Local geometry | "move that wall 600 mm west" | L3 — patch the DSL | zero model | 147 | Drawing only | "show dimensions in cm" | L4 — drawing config | zero model | 148 149 **Options as branches.** When several strategies satisfy a request, each becomes its own git 150 branch with its own sheets, compliance result and cost estimate. Entire captures every agent session and binds it to the commit 164 it produced, so any line of a generated drawing traces back to the conversation that caused 165 it. That is exactly this role and 185 nothing else in the pipeline. The Interviewer and Architect are short structured-output 186 calls — cheaper and more controllable as direct API calls. 187 188 --- 189 190 ## 4. The interview: a grill that cannot invent 191 192 Questions are generated from the ruleset's declared data requirements, and the gap analysis 193 is Python. 194 195 ```yaml 196 # rules/by/residential.yaml 197 - id: BF-TRIGGER-ART48 198 title: Barrier-free dwellings required 199 tier: law 200 source: 201 law: BayBO Art. 48 (1) 202 url: https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/BayBO-48 203 retrieved: 2026-08-22 204 requires: [dwelling_count, storey_count] # ← drives the interview 205 when: dwelling_count > 2 206 then: { require_ruleset: din-18040-2 } 207 ``` 208 209 At interview time the engine computes `needed = ⋃ rule.requires`, subtracts what the brief 210 holds, and asks about the difference. Stop when no **blocking** slot is empty — blocking = required by a `tier: law` rule. 219 Legal inputs are never assumed. 220 2. Cap at 3 rounds, ≤ 4 questions per round. 221 3. Every non-blocking slot still empty is written to `assumptions[]` with its default, basis 222 and confidence, then rendered in the UI as an editable chip. 223 224 The assumption register is the honesty surface: the failure mode of design agents is the 225 silent guess — the model picks 2.50 m ceilings, never mentions it, and the client finds out 226 in the drawing. 227 228 --- 229 230 ## 5. 1	# The Studio — L7, the interface
2	
3	> *"A drawing-office light table. The sheet is the hero; the rest is the instrument
4	> panel."* — the note at the top of the original `style.css`, and still the brief.
5	
6	The Studio is where a person meets the autonomous layer. It has exactly two jobs:
7	take a brief in, and make a building legible coming out. Everything between those
8	two moments happens without it.
9	
10	## Brand
11	
12	Carried forward from the existing UI rather than reinvented — the visual language was
13	already right for the domain and consistency is worth more than novelty.
14	
15	| Token | Value | Role |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `--board` | `#E4E8EC` | the desk the sheet lies on |
18	| `--paper` | `#FFFFFF` | the sheet — always the brightest thing on screen |
19	| `--ink` | `#15191D` | walls, type |
20	| `--accent` | `#2A62D8` | drafting blue: openings, links, the one action |
21	| `--pass` / `--warn` / `--fail` | `#167A4C` / `#B8740A` / `#C8352A` | verdicts, never decoration |
22	| `--font-ui` | Familjen Grotesk | interface |
23	| `--font-mono` | IBM Plex Mono | every number, tag and dimension |
24	
25	Three rules that keep it feeling like a drawing office and not a dashboard:
26	
27	1. **The drawing is the hero.** Panels are quiet; the sheet and the model get the
28	   contrast, the shadow and the space.
29	2. **Numbers are monospace, always.** A room area, a door width, a rule threshold and
30	   a tag are all data, and data lines up.
31	3. **Verdict colour is reserved.** `--pass` / `--fail` mean a compliance result and
32	   nothing else. Nothing decorative is ever green.
33	
34	## The four states
35	
36	### 1 · Brief — the interview
37	
38	Deliberately short. Enough to know intent and the specifications the rules actually
39	need, and not one question more. The whole interview is **five questions**, each with
40	options and a free-text escape:
41	
42	| Question | Why it is asked |
43	|---|---|
44	| What are you building? | selects the building class |
45	| How many homes in it? | **required by BayBO Art. 48** — above two, barrier-free becomes mandatory |
46	| Which rooms, and how many? | the programme |
47	| How big is the plot? | bounds the envelope |
48	| Anything else? | free text, always available |
49	
50	Only questions a `tier: law` rule genuinely needs are blocking. Everything else has a
51	default that is recorded as an **assumption** and shown as an editable chip:
52	
53	```
54	ceiling 2.50 m · assumed · BayBO Art. 45 (1) minimum 2.40 m + 100 mm build-up   ✎
55	```
56	
57	The question list is not hand-written. It is derived from the `requires:` fields of
58	the rules in force, so adding a rule adds its question. See
59	[autonomy.md](autonomy.md) for why this runs *before* the trigger.
60	
61	### 2 · Working
62	
63	The layer stack ticks L2 → L5, each step showing the artifact as it appears. When
64	Devin is running, its own words are shown rather than a spinner — the wait is more
65	tolerable when you can see what it is doing.
66	
67	### 3 · Result
68	
69	Three panes: **3D**, **2D sheet**, **findings**.
70	
71	- **3D** — orbit, zoom, hover a room for its tag and area. Walls, spaces, doors and
72	  windows are separately coloured; doors and windows use the accent so the openings
73	  read at a glance.
74	- **2D** — the generated sheet, the same file that goes to a contractor.
75	- **Findings** — grouped by tier. Every entry links to the statute article it came
76	  from, with the retrieval date. Nothing appears without a citation.
77	
78	The stamp always carries coverage. `PASS 57/57` alone is a lie of omission; the
79	Studio renders `57 checked · 2 not evaluated · 0 failed` and lists what it could not
80	see.
81	
82	### 4 · Options
83	
84	When a run explored several strategies, each is a card with its plan, its verdict and
85	its metrics. The winner is already marked — chosen by the scorer, not by the person
86	looking at the screen. Selecting another is a *new trigger*, not an approval.
87	
88	## How 3D works, and why it is static
89	
90	`ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape` triangulates every wall, space, door and window
91	server-side into `mesh.json` — vertices, faces, tag, class, storey per element. The
92	browser loads that JSON and renders it with Three.js.
93	
94	This approach comes from the Studio work on the `studio` branch and is better than the
95	alternative for our case:
96	
97	| | mesh.json + Three.js | web-ifc (WASM) |
98	|---|---|---|
99	| Parses IFC in the browser | no — already triangulated | yes |
100	| Payload | small, only what is drawn | the whole IFC |
101	| Needs a server at view time | **no** | no |
102	| Element tags and areas | carried in the JSON | must be re-derived |
103	
104	Because meshing happens once, when the artifact is produced, the viewer is a static
105	file reading a static file — which is what makes the whole Studio hostable on GitHub
106	Pages with no backend and no secret in the browser.
107	
108	## Hosting
109	
110	GitHub Pages serves `web/` as static files. A run publishes its artifacts into
111	`web/data/<project>/`, and the Studio reads them:
112	
113	```
114	web/
115	  index.html          the Studio
116	  studio.css          brand tokens + layout
117	  studio.js           viewer, interview, state
118	  data/
119	    index.json        which projects exist
120	    <project>/
121	      mesh.json  sheet.svg  verdict.json  plan.json  design.py
122	```
123	
124	The page never holds a secret. A live run is a `repository_dispatch` posted with the
125	viewer's own credentials, or — for the common case — the Studio simply reads the
126	artifacts a previous run already committed.
127	
128	## What the Studio deliberately does not have
129	
130	No **Approve**, no **Reject**, no **Request changes** on the autonomous path. Those
131	made the previous UI a copilot. A person can start a run and can start another one;
132	they cannot hand-approve a building into existence, because the verifier already
133	decided and it does not need a second opinion.
134

input.command: echo "=== autopilot.yml ===" && cat .github/workflows/autopilot.yml && echo "=== pages.yml ===" && cat .github/workflows/pages.yml
input.description: Read both GitHub Actions workflows

result.output:
=== autopilot.yml ===
# The trigger. Everything after this point runs with nobody in the middle.
#
# Three ways in, all the same pipeline:
#   * repository_dispatch  -- what the web UI posts (the browser holds no secret)
#   * workflow_dispatch    -- a human starting a run from the Actions tab
#   * push to briefs/**    -- committing a brief is itself a trigger
#
# The job never asks for approval. `recognition autopilot` exits non-zero when no
# candidate clears the compliance gate, and that exit code is the gate: a run that
# fails produces no merge, and a run that passes merges itself.
name: autopilot

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [design-request]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      brief:
        description: Path to a DesignBrief JSON in the repo
        required: true
        default: briefs/familienhaus.json
      engine:
        description: local (deterministic) or devin (one session per strategy)
        required: true
        default: local
        type: choice
        options: [local, devin]
      strategies:
        description: Comma-separated subset, blank for all
        required: false
        default: ""
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
    paths: ["briefs/**.json"]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: autopilot-${{ github.event.client_payload.brief || inputs.brief || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  design:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Resolve the trigger
        id: cfg
        run: |
          BRIEF="${{ github.event.client_payload.brief || inputs.brief }}"
          ENGINE="${{ github.event.client_payload.engine || inputs.engine }}"
          STRATS="${{ github.event.client_payload.strategies || inputs.strategies }}"
          # A push to briefs/** carries no inputs: design whatever changed.
          if [ -z "$BRIEF" ]; then
            BRIEF=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD -- 'briefs/*.json' | head -1)
          fi
          [ -z "$BRIEF" ] && BRIEF=briefs/familienhaus.json
          [ -z "$ENGINE" ] && ENGINE=local
          echo "brief=$BRIEF"       >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "engine=$ENGINE"     >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "strategies=$STRATS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "slug=$(basename "$BRIEF" .json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # cairosvg needs the native cairo library; without it sheet rendering dies
      # with a dlopen error that looks nothing like a missing apt package.
      - name: System libraries
        run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq libcairo2

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync

      - name: Verifier must be green before it may design anything
        run: uv run pytest -q

      - name: Autopilot
        id: run
        env:
          DEVIN_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEVIN_API_KEY }}
          DEVIN_ORG_ID: ${{ secrets.DEVIN_ORG_ID }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          uv run recognition autopilot "${{ steps.cfg.outputs.brief }}" \
            --engine "${{ steps.cfg.outputs.engine }}" \
            --out out/autopilot \
            ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.strategies && format('--strategies {0}', steps.cfg.outputs.strategies) || '' }} \
            2>&1 | tee autopilot.log
          echo "winner=$(jq -r '.winner // ""' out/autopilot/*/run.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Publish the artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: design-${{ steps.cfg.outputs.slug }}
          path: |
            out/autopilot/**
            autopilot.log
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # Auto-merge on green. There is no approval step and no Approve button:
      # the deterministic verifier is the only gate, and it has already run.
      - name: Open and merge the winning design
        if: success() && steps.run.outputs.winner != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          SLUG="${{ steps.cfg.outputs.slug }}"
          WINNER="${{ steps.run.outputs.winner }}"
          BRANCH="design/${SLUG}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          git config user.name  "recognition-autopilot"
          git config user.email "autopilot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
          mkdir -p "deliveries/${SLUG}"
          cp -r out/autopilot/*/"${WINNER}"/. "deliveries/${SLUG}/"
          git add "deliveries/${SLUG}"
          git commit -m "design(${SLUG}): ${WINNER} — passed the compliance gate

          Produced by the autopilot with no human in the loop. The winning
          candidate was chosen by recognition.score, not by a person.

# Publish the Studio to GitHub Pages.
#
# The Studio is static: it reads artifacts a run already committed under
# web/data/. So deploying is just uploading web/ — no build step, no server,
# and no secret ever reaches the browser.
#
# Enable once in Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
name: pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["web/**", ".github/workflows/pages.yml"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never cancel a half-finished deploy; let the running one land first.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Fail loudly if the Studio has no data to show
        run: |
          if [ ! -f web/data/index.json ]; then
            echo "::error::web/data/index.json is missing — publish a run first:"
            echo "::error::  uv run recognition autopilot briefs/<name>.json --publish"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "projects:"; jq -r '.projects[] | "  - \(.project) (\(.candidates) layouts, winner: \(.winner))"' web/data/index.json

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: web
      - id: deploy
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

1	"""The autonomous layer: one trigger in, merged artifacts out, nobody in between.
2	
3	    brief ──▶ N candidate strategies ──▶ build each ──▶ verify each
4	                                                          │
5	                        merge the winner ◀── rank ◀───────┘
6	
7	The human is at the *trigger*, never inside the run. Once a brief is sealed the
8	loop runs to a merged pull request with no approval step: the deterministic
9	verifier in `recognition.score` is the only gate, and `score.rank` -- not a person
10	and not a model -- picks which candidate wins.
11	
12	Two candidate engines, same interface:
13	
14	* ``local``  -- strategies are generated by deterministic heuristics here. Fast,
15	  free, always available; used for tests and as the fallback when Devin is
16	  unreachable. This is what makes the system demonstrable without burning ACU.
17	* ``devin``  -- each strategy becomes its own Devin session, working in the repo,
18	  running the verifier on itself, and pushing a branch. Slower, and the real
19	  product: the sessions do the engineering.
20	
21	A run is reproducible: the same brief and the same strategy set produce the same
22	buildings, because everything between the plan and the artifacts is deterministic.
23	"""
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import json
27	import subprocess
28	import sys
29	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
30	from pathlib import Path
31	from typing import Any

33	from .contracts import ArchitectPlan, Adjacency, DesignBrief, Envelope, RoomSpec
34	from .score import Verdict, load_ruleset, rank, verdict, winner
35	from .translate import LayoutError, translate_to_file

37	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

42	# Strategies -- how sibling candidates differ
43	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
44	
45	@dataclass
46	class Strategy:
47	    """One way to satisfy the same brief.
48	
49	    Candidates must differ *structurally*, not by random seed, or the fan-out is
50	    theatre: three sessions producing the same building prove nothing.
51	    """
52	    name: str
53	    label: str
54	    description: str
55	    aspect: float = 1.2          # envelope width : depth
56	    circulation: bool = True     # a dedicated hall spine, or rooms opening directly
57	    generosity: float = 1.0      # multiplier on requested room areas
58	
59	
60	STRATEGIES: list[Strategy] = [
61	    Strategy("compact", "Compact core",
62	             "Squarer envelope with a central hall spine. Least external wall per "
63	             "m2, so cheapest to build and to heat.",
64	             aspect=1.15, circulation=True, generosity=1.0),
65	    Strategy("linear", "Linear frontage",
66	             "Wider, shallower envelope. Every habitable room reaches an exterior "
67	             "wall, which makes the daylight rule easy to satisfy.",
68	             aspect=1.75, circulation=True, generosity=1.0),
69	    Strategy("open", "Open plan",
70	             "No dedicated corridor; living spaces connect directly. Converts "
71	             "circulation area into usable floor.",
72	             aspect=1.35, circulation=False, generosity=1.12),
73	]
74	
75	
76	def strategy_by_name(name: str) -> Strategy:
77	    for s in STRATEGIES:
78	        if s.name == name:
79	            return s
80	    raise KeyError(f"unknown strategy '{name}'; have {[s.name for s in STRATEGIES]}")

84	# Brief -> ArchitectPlan (the `local` candidate engine)
85	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
86	
87	DEFAULT_AREAS = {          # Richtwerte, guidance tier -- never presented as law
88	    "living": 26.0, "kitchen": 12.0, "bedroom": 14.0, "bathroom": 8.0,
89	    "office": 12.0, "hall": 10.0, "utility": 6.0, "other": 10.0,
90	}

93	def plan_from_brief(brief: DesignBrief, strat: Strategy) -> ArchitectPlan:
94	    """Deterministically expand a brief into a plan under one strategy.
95	
96	    No model is called. Room areas come from the brief where the client gave
97	    them and from published Richtwerte otherwise -- and because those are
98	    guidance, not law, the compliance gate will never block on them.
99	    """
100	    rooms: list[RoomSpec] = []
101	    n = 0
102	    for req in brief.rooms:
103	        for i in range(req.count):
104	            n += 1
105	            base = req.min_area_m2 or DEFAULT_AREAS.get(req.category, 12.0)
106	            label = req.label or _german(req.category)
107	            if req.count > 1:
108	                label = f"{label} {i + 1}"
109	            rooms.append(RoomSpec(
110	                id=f"R-{n:02d}", category=req.category, label=label,
111	                target_area_m2=round(base * strat.generosity, 1),
112	            ))
113	
114	    hall_id: str | None = None
115	    if strat.circulation and not any(r.category == "hall" for r in rooms):
116	        n += 1
117	        hall_id = f"R-{n:02d}"
118	        rooms.append(RoomSpec(hall_id, "hall", "Flur",
119	                              round(DEFAULT_AREAS["hall"] * strat.generosity, 1)))
120	    elif strat.circulation:
121	        hall_id = next(r.id for r in rooms if r.category == "hall")
122	
123	    # Envelope sized from the programme plus a circulation and wall allowance,
124	    # then shaped by the strategy's aspect ratio.
125	    need = sum(r.target_area_m2 for r in rooms) * 1.22
126	    depth = (need / strat.aspect) ** 0.5
127	    width = need / depth
128	    env = Envelope(width_m=round(width * 2) / 2, depth_m=round(depth * 2) / 2)
129	
130	    adjacency = _adjacencies(rooms, hall_id)
131	    return ArchitectPlan(
132	        project=brief.project, envelope=env, rooms=rooms, adjacency=adjacency,
133	        storey_height_m=brief.storey_height_m, circulation_id=hall_id,
134	        accessibility_tier=brief.accessibility_tier,
135	        rationale=f"{strat.label}: {strat.description}",
136	    )

139	def _adjacencies(rooms: list[RoomSpec], hall_id: str | None) -> list[Adjacency]:
140	    """Everything opens off the hall; without one, chain through the living room.
141	
142	    A bathroom is never reached through a bedroom -- that is the convention this
143	    codifies, and it is why adjacency is declared rather than inferred later.
144	    """
145	    if hall_id:
146	        return [Adjacency(hall_id, r.id) for r in rooms if r.id != hall_id]
147	    anchor = next((r for r in rooms if r.category == "living"), rooms[0])
148	    return [Adjacency(anchor.id, r.id) for r in rooms if r.id != anchor.id]
149

152	    return {"living": "Wohnen", "kitchen": "Küche", "bedroom": "Schlafzimmer",
153	            "bathroom": "Bad", "office": "Büro", "hall": "Flur",
154	            "utility": "HWR", "other": "Raum"}.get(category, category.title())

164	    label: str

166	    out_dir: Path | None = None
167	    verdict: Verdict | None = None

179	            "ok": self.ok, "error": self.error,

185	def build_and_verify(plan: ArchitectPlan, out_dir: Path, *, name: str,
186	                     rules_path: Path = DEFAULT_RULES,
187	                     brief: DesignBrief | None = None,
188	                     viewable: bool = True) -> Verdict:
189	    """Plan -> DSL -> IFC -> compliance verdict. Every step deterministic.

191	    With `viewable`, also renders the sheets and the 3D mesh the Studio needs.
192	    Tests turn it off: geometry is the thing under test, rendering is not.
193	    """
194	    import recognition.model as M
195	    import recognition.rules as R
196	
197	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
198	    plan.write(out_dir / "plan.json")
199	
200	    dsl = translate_to_file(plan, out_dir / "design.py")           # L3: zero tokens
201	    ifc_path = out_dir / "model.ifc"
202	    _exec_dsl(dsl, ifc_path)                                       # L4: geometry

210	                metrics=_metrics(plan, model))

213	    if viewable:

219	    """Sheets and the 3D mesh: everything a person needs to judge the result.

221	    Best-effort by design. A candidate is legal or not on the strength of its
222	    compliance verdict; a missing PNG must never turn a passing building into a
223	    failing one, so rendering problems are reported and swallowed.

227	    try:

229	    except Exception as e:                      # noqa: BLE001 - presentation only
230	        print(f"      (sheets unavailable: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:90]})")
231	    try:

237	def _exec_dsl(dsl_path: Path, ifc_path: Path) -> None:
238	    """Run the generated module in a subprocess so a bad candidate cannot take
239	    the orchestrator down with it."""
240	    ifc_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
241	    code = (
242	        f"import runpy,sys;"
243	        f"ns=runpy.run_path({str(dsl_path)!r});"
244	        f"ns['h'].write({str(ifc_path)!r})"
245	    )
246	    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], cwd=REPO_ROOT,
247	                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
248	    if proc.returncode != 0 or not ifc_path.exists():
249	        raise RuntimeError(
250	            f"generated design failed to build an IFC:\n{proc.stderr[-1500:]}"
251	        )

254	def _metrics(plan: ArchitectPlan, model) -> dict[str, Any]:
255	    """Ranking inputs. Cheap, geometric, and free of judgement."""
256	    room_area = sum(s.area for s in model.spaces)
257	    circ = sum(s.area for s in model.spaces if s.category == "hall")
258	    env = plan.envelope.area_m2
259	    return {
260	        "envelope_m2": round(env, 2),
261	        "room_area_m2": round(room_area, 2),
262	        "usable_ratio": round((room_area - circ) / env, 4) if env else 0.0,
263	        "circulation_m2": round(circ, 2),
264	        "openings": len(model.doors) + len(model.windows),
265	        "rooms": len(model.spaces),
266	    }

273	@dataclass
274	class RunResult:
275	    project: str
276	    engine: str
277	    candidates: list[Candidate] = field(default_factory=list)
278	    winner: str = ""
279	    merged: str = ""

285	            "winner": self.winner, "merged": self.merged, "critic": self.critic,
286	            "candidates": [c.summary() for c in self.candidates],

289	    def write(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
290	        p = Path(path)
291	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
292	        p.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

296	def run_local(brief: DesignBrief, out_root: Path, *, strategies: list[Strategy] | None = None,
297	              rules_path: Path = DEFAULT_RULES, log=print) -> RunResult:
298	    """The full loop with deterministic candidate generation. No API, no cost."""
299	    brief.resolve_accessibility()
300	    brief.validate()
301	    strats = strategies or STRATEGIES
302	    res = RunResult(project=brief.project, engine="local")
303	
304	    for strat in strats:
305	        c = Candidate(strat.name, strat.label)
306	        log(f"  · {strat.name}: {strat.description[:64]}…")
307	        try:
308	            plan = plan_from_brief(brief, strat)
309	            c.plan = plan
310	            c.out_dir = out_root / strat.name
311	            c.verdict = build_and_verify(plan, c.out_dir, name=strat.name,
312	                                         rules_path=rules_path, brief=brief)
313	            log(f"    {c.verdict.stamp()} — {c.verdict.coverage_line()}")
314	        except (LayoutError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as e:
315	            # A candidate that cannot be built is a legitimate outcome of
316	            # exploration, not a crash. Record it and keep the siblings running.
317	            c.error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
318	            log(f"    unbuildable — {c.error[:110]}")
319	        res.candidates.append(c)
320	
321	    verdicts = [c.verdict for c in res.candidates if c.verdict]
322	    best = winner(verdicts)
323	    if best:
324	        res.winner = best.candidate
325	        log(f"\n  winner: {best.candidate} ({best.coverage_line()}) — chosen by the scorer, not a human")
326	    else:
327	        log("\n  no candidate passed the compliance gate")
328	    res.write(out_root / "run.json")

340	BUILDER_PROMPT = """\

342	layout as an ArchitectPlan JSON object and return it via the structured output
343	tool. Do not write code, do not open a pull request, and do not push anything.
344

355	  rooms:    [{{id: "R-01", category, label, target_area_m2, exterior_wall}}]
356	  adjacency:[{{a: "R-03", b: "R-01", via: "door"}}]
357	  circulation_id: the id of the hall room, or null for an open plan

361	1. NO COORDINATES. Give areas and adjacencies only. Wall positions are computed
362	   downstream by deterministic code; anything you invent there is discarded.
363	2. category must be one of: bedroom, living, kitchen, bathroom, office, hall,

366	   bathroom is never reached through a bedroom.
367	4. Sum of target_area_m2 must fit the envelope with ~22% left for walls and
368	   circulation, or the plan is infeasible and will be thrown away.

382	{plan}
383

395	def run_devin(brief: DesignBrief, out_root: Path, *,
396	              strategies: list[Strategy] | None = None,
397	              rules_path: Path = DEFAULT_RULES,

399	              critic: bool = True, log=print) -> RunResult:

401	
402	    Devin returns an ArchitectPlan and never touches the repository. That is not
403	    a workaround for the missing write permission -- it is the safer split. The
404	    session cannot report its own success, because the artifacts it is judged on
405	    are produced here, by deterministic code, from the plan it handed back.
406	    """
407	    from .devin import DevinClient, SessionSpec, fan_out, wait_all
408	
409	    brief.resolve_accessibility()
410	    brief.validate()
411	    strats = strategies or STRATEGIES
412	    res = RunResult(project=brief.project, engine="devin")
413	    client = DevinClient()
414	
415	    brief_json = json.dumps(brief.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
416	    specs = [

418	            name=s.name, strategy=s.name,
419	            prompt=BUILDER_PROMPT.format(label=s.label, description=s.description,
420	                                         brief=brief_json),
421	            tags=["recognition", "autopilot", f"strategy:{s.name}"],
422	            max_acu=max_acu,

432	    def _tick(name: str, snap) -> None:
433	        log(f"    {name:9} … {snap.status}")

435	    results = wait_all(client, ids, timeout_s=timeout_s, on_update=_tick)
436

440	        c.devin_session = r.session_id if r else ""
441	        if r is None or not r.produced_output:
442	            c.error = (r.error if r else "no result") or f"session ended in '{r.status}' with no plan"
443	            log(f"  · {s.name}: {c.error[:110]}")
444	            res.candidates.append(c)
445	            continue
446	        try:
447	            plan, out = _plan_with_repair(client, r, brief, s, timeout_s, log=log)
448	            c.plan = plan
449	            c.out_dir = out_root / s.name
450	            c.verdict = build_and_verify(plan, c.out_dir, name=s.name,
451	                                         rules_path=rules_path, brief=brief)
452	            log(f"  · {s.name}: {c.verdict.stamp()} — {c.verdict.coverage_line()}")
453	        except (LayoutError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as e:
454	            c.error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
455	            log(f"  · {s.name}: unbuildable — {c.error[:110]}")
456	        res.candidates.append(c)
457	
458	    best = winner([c.verdict for c in res.candidates if c.verdict])
459	    if best:
460	        res.winner = best.candidate
461	        log(f"\n  winner: {best.candidate} — chosen by the scorer, not a human")
462	        if critic:
463	            res.critic = _run_critic(client, res, best, log=log)
464	    else:
465	        log("\n  no candidate passed the compliance gate")
466	
467	    client.close()
468	    res.write(out_root / "run.json")
469	    return res

472	def _plan_with_repair(client, result, brief: DesignBrief, strat: Strategy,
473	                      timeout_s: float, *, attempts: int = 2, log=print) -> tuple[ArchitectPlan, dict]:
474	    """Validate the session's plan; on a contract error, hand the error back.
475	
476	    This is the whole autonomy argument in miniature. The validator's message is
477	    written to be an instruction ("room R-04 target_area_m2 must be > 0"), so the
478	    session can repair itself without a human reading the traceback. No person
479	    sees this loop unless every attempt fails.
480	    """
481	    from .contracts import ContractError
482	    from .devin import wait_all
483	
484	    payload = result.structured_output
485	    last_err = ""
486	    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
487	        try:
488	            return _plan_from_output(payload, brief, strat, log=log), payload
489	        except ContractError as e:
490	            last_err = str(e)
491	            if attempt == attempts:
492	                break
493	            log(f"    {strat.name}: contract error, asking the session to repair "
494	                f"(attempt {attempt}/{attempts - 1})")
495	            log(f"      {last_err[:150]}")
496	            try:
497	                client.send_message(
498	                    result.session_id,
499	                    f"The plan you returned was rejected by the schema validator:\n\n"
500	                    f"  {last_err}\n\n"
501	                    f"Return the corrected ArchitectPlan JSON object only. Change nothing "
502	                    f"except what the error names."
503	                )
504	            except Exception as e2:            # noqa: BLE001 - repair is best effort
505	                log(f"      could not send repair request: {e2}")
506	                break
507	            nxt = wait_all(client, {strat.name: result.session_id},
508	                           timeout_s=min(timeout_s, 600)).get(strat.name)
509	            if not nxt or not nxt.structured_output:
510	                break
511	            payload = nxt.structured_output
512	    raise ValueError(f"plan rejected after {attempts} attempt(s): {last_err}")
513

515	def _plan_schema() -> dict:
516	    """The structured-output contract handed to every builder session."""
517	    return {
518	        "type": "object",
519	        "properties": {
520	            "envelope": {"type": "object"},
521	            "rooms": {"type": "array"},
522	            "adjacency": {"type": "array"},
523	            "circulation_id": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
524	            "storey_height_m": {"type": "number"},
525	            "accessibility_tier": {"type": "string"},
526	            "rationale": {"type": "string"},
527	        },
528	        "required": ["envelope", "rooms"],
529	    }
530	
531	
532	# Synonyms observed from real sessions. Normalising these is being liberal about
533	# vocabulary, not about meaning: each maps to exactly one term with no ambiguity.
534	# Anything genuinely wrong still fails validation and goes back for repair.
535	_VIA_SYNONYMS = {"opening": "open", "open_plan": "open", "openplan": "open",
536	                 "direct": "open", "doorway": "door", "passage": "open"}
537	_CATEGORY_SYNONYMS = {
538	    "bath": "bathroom", "wc": "bathroom", "toilet": "bathroom", "shower": "bathroom",
539	    "bed": "bedroom", "bedrooms": "bedroom", "sleeping": "bedroom",
540	    "livingroom": "living", "living_room": "living", "lounge": "living", "dining": "living",
541	    "corridor": "hall", "hallway": "hall", "flur": "hall", "circulation": "hall",
542	    "study": "office", "workroom": "office",
543	    "storage": "utility", "technical": "utility", "laundry": "utility", "hwr": "utility",
544	}
545	
546	
547	def normalise_agent_plan(payload: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
548	    """Map known vocabulary variants onto the contract's terms.
549	
550	    Returns the payload plus a list of what was rewritten, so normalisation is
551	    visible in the run log rather than being a silent correction.
552	    """
553	    notes: list[str] = []
554	    for a in payload.get("adjacency", []) or []:
555	        if not isinstance(a, dict):
556	            continue
557	        via = str(a.get("via", "door")).strip().lower()
558	        if via in _VIA_SYNONYMS:
559	            notes.append(f"adjacency via '{via}' → '{_VIA_SYNONYMS[via]}'")
560	            a["via"] = _VIA_SYNONYMS[via]
561	    for r in payload.get("rooms", []) or []:
562	        if not isinstance(r, dict):
563	            continue
564	        cat = str(r.get("category", "")).strip().lower().replace(" ", "_")
565	        if cat in _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS:
566	            notes.append(f"room {r.get('id')} category '{cat}' → '{_CATEGORY_SYNONYMS[cat]}'")
567	            r["category"] = _CATEGORY_SYNONYMS[cat]
568	        elif cat:
569	            r["category"] = cat
570	    return payload, notes
571	
572	
573	def _plan_from_output(out: dict, brief: DesignBrief, strat: Strategy,
574	                      log=None) -> ArchitectPlan:
575	    """Validate whatever the session returned. Never trust it unchecked."""
576	    from .contracts import load_plan
577	    payload = dict(out)
578	    payload.setdefault("project", brief.project)
579	    payload.setdefault("storey_height_m", brief.storey_height_m)
580	    payload.setdefault("accessibility_tier", brief.accessibility_tier)
581	    payload.setdefault("rationale", f"{strat.label}: {strat.description}")
582	    payload.pop("schema", None)
583	    payload, notes = normalise_agent_plan(payload)
584	    if notes and log:
585	        for n in notes:
586	            log(f"      normalised: {n}")
587	    return load_plan(payload)

590	def _run_critic(client, res: RunResult, best: Verdict, *, log=print) -> str:
591	    """A fourth session that reviews what the checker cannot see.
592	
593	    Advisory by construction: it can annotate the winner, never overturn it. A
594	    model must not be able to veto a deterministic gate, in either direction.
595	    """
596	    from .devin import wait_all
597	    cand = next((c for c in res.candidates if c.verdict is best), None)
598	    if cand is None or cand.plan is None:
599	        return ""
600	    log("  critic: reviewing the winner…")
601	    try:
602	        sid = client.create_session(
603	            CRITIC_PROMPT.format(
604	                plan=json.dumps(cand.plan.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)[:6000],
605	                verdict=json.dumps(best.to_dict()["findings"][:10], indent=2)[:3000],
606	            ),
607	            title=f"Recognition · critic · {res.project}",
608	            tags=["recognition", "autopilot", "critic"],
609	            structured_output={"type": "object",
610	                               "properties": {"verdict": {"type": "string"},
611	                                              "notes": {"type": "string"}},
612	                               "required": ["verdict", "notes"]},
613	        )
614	    except Exception as e:                     # noqa: BLE001 - advisory stage
615	        log(f"  critic unavailable: {e}")
616	        return ""
617	    out = wait_all(client, {"critic": sid}, timeout_s=900).get("critic")
618	    if out and out.structured_output:
619	        note = str(out.structured_output.get("notes", ""))[:1200]
620	        log(f"  critic says: {note[:160]}")
621	        return note
622	    return ""

1	"""ArchitectPlan -> design DSL source. Deterministic, zero language-model tokens.
2	
3	This module is the reason the system does not hallucinate geometry. The agent
4	supplies relationships and areas; every coordinate in the resulting building is
5	computed here, by code you can read, from numbers the agent had to justify.
6	
7	The pattern is borrowed from Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD (MIT), whose deterministic
8	`_plan_to_code` translator carried most of its 116x token reduction *and* a higher
9	pass rate than the LLM-writes-code baseline. Determinism improved quality; it was
10	not a trade against it.
11	
12	Layout algorithm
13	----------------
14	Squarified treemap over the interior rectangle. Rooms are placed in rows whose
15	aspect ratios are kept as close to 1 as possible, because a 1.2 x 18 m bedroom is
16	technically the right area and architecturally useless. Circulation is placed
17	first as a spine so every room can open onto it.
18	
19	Everything snaps to a 5 cm grid: real buildings are dimensioned in round numbers,
20	and snapping keeps generated diffs stable across runs.
21	
22	What it cannot express -- curved walls, split levels, non-rectangular envelopes --
23	becomes a `# TODO_AGENT:` marker carrying the plan fragment. Those markers are the
24	only geometry an agent is ever asked to write, and they show up in the diff.
25	"""
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import math
29	from dataclasses import dataclass
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	from .contracts import ArchitectPlan, RoomSpec
33	
34	GRID = 0.05           # 5 cm
35	MIN_SIDE = 1.20       # a room narrower than this is not a room
36	MIN_DOOR_WALL = 1.00  # a shared edge shorter than this cannot host a door
37	# DIN 18040-2 wants 1.20 m of *clear* corridor. The spine is laid out on wall
38	# centre-lines and the room polygon is then inset by half a partition on each
39	# side, so the centre-line strip must carry a full wall thickness of slack or the
40	# finished corridor measures ~1.10 m and fails the very rule it was sized for.
41	CORRIDOR_CLEAR = 1.20
42	CORRIDOR_MIN = CORRIDOR_CLEAR + 0.15
43	
44	
45	def snap(v: float, grid: float = GRID) -> float:
46	    return round(round(v / grid) * grid, 3)
47	
48	
49	@dataclass
50	class Rect:
51	    """Axis-aligned room footprint in storey coordinates (x east, y north)."""
52	    x: float
53	    y: float
54	    w: float
55	    h: float
56	
57	    @property
58	    def x2(self) -> float:
59	        return self.x + self.w
60	
61	    @property
62	    def y2(self) -> float:
63	        return self.y + self.h
64	
65	    @property
66	    def area(self) -> float:
67	        return self.w * self.h
68	
69	    @property
70	    def aspect(self) -> float:
71	        lo, hi = sorted((self.w, self.h))
72	        return hi / lo if lo > 0 else math.inf
73	
74	    def polygon(self) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
75	        return [(self.x, self.y), (self.x2, self.y), (self.x2, self.y2), (self.x, self.y2)]
76	
77	    def snapped(self) -> Rect:
78	        x, y = snap(self.x), snap(self.y)
79	        return Rect(x, y, snap(self.x2) - x, snap(self.y2) - y)
80	
81	
82	class LayoutError(RuntimeError):
83	    """Packing could not satisfy the plan. Returned to L2, never passed downstream."""
84	
85	
86	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	# Squarified treemap
88	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	
90	def _worst(row: list[float], side: float, scale: float) -> float:
91	    """Worst aspect ratio in a row laid along `side` (van Wijk et al.)."""
92	    if not row or side <= 0:
93	        return math.inf
94	    total = sum(row) * scale
95	    if total <= 0:
96	        return math.inf
97	    breadth = total / side
98	    return max(max(breadth / (a * scale / breadth) if a > 0 else math.inf,
99	                   (a * scale / breadth) / breadth if a > 0 else math.inf)
100	               for a in row)
101	
102	
103	def squarify(areas: list[float], rect: Rect) -> list[Rect]:
104	    """Lay out `areas` inside `rect`, keeping each cell as square as possible."""
105	    if not areas:
106	        return []
107	    scale = rect.area / sum(areas)
108	    out: list[Rect] = []
109	    free = Rect(rect.x, rect.y, rect.w, rect.h)
110	    remaining = list(areas)
111	    row: list[float] = []
112	
113	    while remaining:
114	        side = min(free.w, free.h)
115	        candidate = row + [remaining[0]]
116	        if not row or _worst(candidate, side, scale) <= _worst(row, side, scale):
117	            row.append(remaining.pop(0))
118	            continue
119	        out.extend(_place_row(row, free, scale))
120	        free = _shrink(free, row, scale)
121	        row = []
122	
123	    if row:
124	        out.extend(_place_row(row, free, scale))
125	    return out
126	
127	
128	def _place_row(row: list[float], free: Rect, scale: float) -> list[Rect]:
129	    total = sum(row) * scale
130	    cells: list[Rect] = []
131	    if free.w <= free.h:                      # lay the row horizontally
132	        height = total / free.w if free.w else 0.0
133	        x = free.x
134	        for a in row:
135	            w = (a * scale) / height if height else 0.0
136	            cells.append(Rect(x, free.y, w, height))
137	            x += w
138	    else:                                     # lay the row vertically
139	        width = total / free.h if free.h else 0.0
140	        y = free.y
141	        for a in row:
142	            h = (a * scale) / width if width else 0.0
143	            cells.append(Rect(free.x, y, width, h))
144	            y += h
145	    return cells
146	
147	
148	def _shrink(free: Rect, row: list[float], scale: float) -> Rect:
149	    total = sum(row) * scale
150	    if free.w <= free.h:
151	        height = total / free.w if free.w else 0.0
152	        return Rect(free.x, free.y + height, free.w, free.h - height)
153	    width = total / free.h if free.h else 0.0
154	    return Rect(free.x + width, free.y, free.w - width, free.h)
155	
156	
157	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
158	# Plan -> rectangles
159	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
160	
161	def layout(plan: ArchitectPlan) -> dict[str, Rect]:
162	    """Assign every room an axis-aligned footprint inside the envelope.
163	
164	    Circulation, if the plan names one, is laid out as a spine strip across the
165	    interior so that every other room has a boundary to open a door onto.
166	    """
167	    e = plan.envelope
168	    half = e.external_wall_m / 2.0
169	    inner = Rect(half, half, e.width_m - e.external_wall_m, e.depth_m - e.external_wall_m)
170	    if inner.w <= 0 or inner.h <= 0:
171	        raise LayoutError(
172	            f"envelope {e.width_m} x {e.depth_m} m is smaller than its own external walls"
173	        )
174	
175	    rooms = list(plan.rooms)
176	    rects: dict[str, Rect] = {}
177	
178	    spine = plan.circulation_id
179	    if spine and len(rooms) > 1:
180	        hall = plan.room(spine)
181	        others = [r for r in rooms if r.id != spine]
182	        # Spine runs along the longer axis; depth from its area, floored at a
183	        # width a person can actually pass through (DIN 18040-2 wants 1.20 m).
184	        if inner.w >= inner.h:
185	            depth = max(hall.target_area_m2 / inner.w, CORRIDOR_MIN)
186	            depth = min(depth, inner.h * 0.5)
187	            y = inner.y + (inner.h - depth) / 2.0
188	            rects[spine] = Rect(inner.x, y, inner.w, depth)
189	            bands = [Rect(inner.x, inner.y, inner.w, y - inner.y),
190	                     Rect(inner.x, y + depth, inner.w, inner.y2 - (y + depth))]
191	        else:
192	            depth = max(hall.target_area_m2 / inner.h, CORRIDOR_MIN)
193	            depth = min(depth, inner.w * 0.5)
194	            x = inner.x + (inner.w - depth) / 2.0
195	            rects[spine] = Rect(x, inner.y, depth, inner.h)
196	            bands = [Rect(inner.x, inner.y, x - inner.x, inner.h),
197	                     Rect(x + depth, inner.y, inner.x2 - (x + depth), inner.h)]
198	        rects.update(_fill_bands(others, bands))
199	    else:
200	        for r, cell in zip(rooms, squarify([x.target_area_m2 for x in rooms], inner)):
201	            rects[r.id] = cell
202	
203	    out = {k: v.snapped() for k, v in rects.items()}
204	    _assert_sane(out, plan)
205	    return out
206	
207	
208	def _fill_bands(rooms: list[RoomSpec], bands: list[Rect]) -> dict[str, Rect]:
209	    """Distribute rooms across the bands either side of the spine, by area."""
210	    usable = [b for b in bands if b.w > 0.01 and b.h > 0.01]
211	    if not usable:
212	        raise LayoutError("no usable floor area remains beside the circulation spine")
213	
214	    order = sorted(rooms, key=lambda r: -r.target_area_m2)
215	    buckets: list[list[RoomSpec]] = [[] for _ in usable]
216	    load = [0.0] * len(usable)
217	    caps = [b.area for b in usable]
218	    for r in order:                       # greedy: fill whichever band is least full
219	        i = min(range(len(usable)), key=lambda j: load[j] / caps[j] if caps[j] else math.inf)
220	        buckets[i].append(r)
221	        load[i] += r.target_area_m2
222	
223	    out: dict[str, Rect] = {}
224	    for band, group in zip(usable, buckets):
225	        if not group:
226	            continue
227	        for r, cell in zip(group, squarify([x.target_area_m2 for x in group], band)):
228	            out[r.id] = cell
229	    return out
230	
231	
232	def _assert_sane(rects: dict[str, Rect], plan: ArchitectPlan) -> None:
233	    for rid, r in rects.items():
234	        # Tolerance matters: a corridor snapped to exactly 1.20 m can land at
235	        # 1.19999... in floating point and must not be rejected as too narrow.
236	        if min(r.w, r.h) < MIN_SIDE - 1e-6:
237	            raise LayoutError(
238	                f"room {rid} came out {r.w:.2f} x {r.h:.2f} m; its narrow side is below "
239	                f"{MIN_SIDE} m. Give it more area, or reduce the number of rooms sharing "
240	                f"the {plan.envelope.width_m} x {plan.envelope.depth_m} m envelope."
241	            )
242	    ids = list(rects)
243	    for i, a in enumerate(ids):
244	        for b in ids[i + 1:]:
245	            ra, rb = rects[a], rects[b]
246	            ox = min(ra.x2, rb.x2) - max(ra.x, rb.x)
247	            oy = min(ra.y2, rb.y2) - max(ra.y, rb.y)
248	            if ox > 0.01 and oy > 0.01:
249	                raise LayoutError(f"rooms {a} and {b} overlap by {ox:.2f} x {oy:.2f} m")
250

256	@dataclass
257	class WallSeg:
258	    name: str
259	    start: tuple[float, float]
260	    end: tuple[float, float]
261	    thickness: float
262	    external: bool
263	
264	    @property
265	    def length(self) -> float:
266	        return math.dist(self.start, self.end)
267	
268	
269	def shared_edge(a: Rect, b: Rect) -> tuple[str, float, float, float] | None:
270	    """Return (axis, coord, lo, hi) of the boundary a and b share, if any."""
271	    tol = 0.02
272	    if abs(a.x2 - b.x) < tol or abs(b.x2 - a.x) < tol:      # vertical contact
273	        coord = a.x2 if abs(a.x2 - b.x) < tol else b.x2
274	        lo, hi = max(a.y, b.y), min(a.y2, b.y2)
275	        if hi - lo > MIN_DOOR_WALL:
276	            return ("x", coord, lo, hi)
277	    if abs(a.y2 - b.y) < tol or abs(b.y2 - a.y) < tol:      # horizontal contact
278	        coord = a.y2 if abs(a.y2 - b.y) < tol else b.y2
279	        lo, hi = max(a.x, b.x), min(a.x2, b.x2)
280	        if hi - lo > MIN_DOOR_WALL:
281	            return ("y", coord, lo, hi)
282	    return None
283	
284	
285	def build_walls(plan: ArchitectPlan, rects: dict[str, Rect]) -> list[WallSeg]:
286	    """External envelope walls plus one internal partition per shared boundary."""
287	    e = plan.envelope
288	    W, D = e.width_m, e.depth_m
289	    half = e.external_wall_m / 2.0
290	    walls = [
291	        WallSeg("EXT-S", (half, half), (W - half, half), e.external_wall_m, True),
292	        WallSeg("EXT-E", (W - half, half), (W - half, D - half), e.external_wall_m, True),
293	        WallSeg("EXT-N", (W - half, D - half), (half, D - half), e.external_wall_m, True),
294	        WallSeg("EXT-W", (half, D - half), (half, half), e.external_wall_m, True),
295	    ]
296	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
297	    ids = sorted(rects)
298	    n = 0
299	    for i, a in enumerate(ids):
300	        for b in ids[i + 1:]:
301	            edge = shared_edge(rects[a], rects[b])
302	            if not edge:
303	                continue
304	            axis, coord, lo, hi = edge
305	            key = (axis, round(coord, 2), round(lo, 2), round(hi, 2))
306	            if key in seen:
307	                continue
308	            seen.add(key)
309	            n += 1
310	            if axis == "x":
311	                seg = WallSeg(f"INT-{n}", (coord, lo), (coord, hi), e.internal_wall_m, False)
312	            else:
313	                seg = WallSeg(f"INT-{n}", (lo, coord), (hi, coord), e.internal_wall_m, False)
314	            walls.append(seg)
315	    return walls
316	
317	
318	def _wall_for(walls: list[WallSeg], axis: str, coord: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> WallSeg | None:
319	    tol = 0.05
320	    mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
321	    for w in walls:
322	        horizontal = abs(w.start[1] - w.end[1]) < tol
323	        if axis == "y" and horizontal and abs(w.start[1] - coord) < tol:
324	            if min(w.start[0], w.end[0]) - tol <= mid <= max(w.start[0], w.end[0]) + tol:
325	                return w
326	        if axis == "x" and not horizontal and abs(w.start[0] - coord) < tol:
327	            if min(w.start[1], w.end[1]) - tol <= mid <= max(w.start[1], w.end[1]) + tol:
328	                return w
329	    return None
330	
331	
332	def _offset_along(wall: WallSeg, point: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
333	    """Distance from the wall's start to `point`, as the DSL's `at` expects."""
334	    return math.dist(wall.start, point)

341	HEADER = '''"""{project} -- generated by recognition.translate. Do not edit by hand.
342	
343	Regenerate with:  uv run recognition build plans/{slug}.json
344	
345	Every coordinate below was computed from the ArchitectPlan by deterministic code,
346	not written by a language model. Change the plan, not this file.
347	"""
348	from recognition.design import House
349	
350	h = House({project!r})
351	eg = h.storey({storey!r}, elevation=0.0, height={height})
352	'''

355	def door_width(tier: str, external: bool) -> float:
356	    """DIN 18040-2 clear widths when a barrier-free tier is in force."""
357	    if tier == "din18040_2_R":
358	        return 0.90
359	    if tier == "din18040_2":
360	        return 0.90 if external else 0.80
361	    return 1.01 if external else 0.885

364	def emit(plan: ArchitectPlan, rects: dict[str, Rect], walls: list[WallSeg]) -> str:
365	    """Render the DSL source. Pure string building -- no model, no randomness."""
366	    slug = plan.project.lower().replace(" ", "-")
367	    lines = [HEADER.format(project=plan.project, slug=slug,
368	                           storey=plan.storey_name, height=plan.storey_height_m)]
369	
370	    lines.append("\n# --- walls: external envelope, then partitions between rooms ---")
371	    for w in walls:
372	        lines.append(
373	            f"eg.wall({w.name!r}, ({snap(w.start[0])}, {snap(w.start[1])}), "
374	            f"({snap(w.end[0])}, {snap(w.end[1])}), thickness={w.thickness}"
375	            + (", external=True)" if w.external else ")")
376	        )
377	
378	    lines.append("\n# --- rooms: floor outlines inset to the inside face of their walls ---")
379	    e = plan.envelope
380	    for r in plan.rooms:
381	        rect = rects[r.id]
382	        inset = _inset(rect, plan, e)
383	        pts = ", ".join(f"({snap(x)}, {snap(y)})" for x, y in inset.polygon())
384	        lines.append(f"eg.room({r.label!r}, [{pts}])   # {r.id} {rect.area:.1f} m2 target {r.target_area_m2:.1f}")
385	
386	    tier = plan.accessibility_tier
387	    lines.append("\n# --- doors: one per adjacency declared in the plan ---")
388	    lines.extend(_emit_doors(plan, rects, walls, tier))
389	
390	    lines.append("\n# --- windows: sized to the daylight rule, on exterior walls ---")
391	    lines.extend(_emit_windows(plan, rects, walls))
392	
393	    if plan.todo_agent:
394	        lines.append("\n# --- constructs the translator cannot express ---")
395	        lines.extend(f"# TODO_AGENT: {t}" for t in plan.todo_agent)
396	
397	    lines.append(f'\nif __name__ == "__main__":\n    h.write("out/{slug}/model.ifc")\n')
398	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

401	def _inset(rect: Rect, plan: ArchitectPlan, e) -> Rect:
402	    """Pull a room footprint back to the inside face of whatever wall bounds it."""
403	    def d(on_envelope: bool) -> float:
404	        return e.external_wall_m / 2.0 if on_envelope else e.internal_wall_m / 2.0
405	    tol = 0.02
406	    half = e.external_wall_m / 2.0
407	    left = d(abs(rect.x - half) < tol)
408	    right = d(abs(rect.x2 - (e.width_m - half)) < tol)
409	    bottom = d(abs(rect.y - half) < tol)
410	    top = d(abs(rect.y2 - (e.depth_m - half)) < tol)
411	    return Rect(rect.x + left, rect.y + bottom,
412	                rect.w - left - right, rect.h - bottom - top)
413	
414	
415	def _nearest_neighbour(room_id: str, rects: dict[str, Rect], exclude: set[str]
416	                       ) -> tuple[str, tuple | None]:
417	    """The neighbour sharing the longest usable wall with `room_id`.
418	
419	    Longest wins because a wider shared boundary is the more natural place to
420	    hang a door, and because it is a stable, deterministic choice.
421	    """
422	    best_id, best_edge, best_len = "", None, 0.0
423	    for other in rects:
424	        if other == room_id or other in exclude - {room_id}:
425	            continue
426	        if other == room_id:
427	            continue
428	        edge = shared_edge(rects[other], rects[room_id])
429	        if edge is None:
430	            continue
431	        _axis, _coord, lo, hi = edge
432	        if hi - lo > best_len:
433	            best_id, best_edge, best_len = other, edge, hi - lo
434	    return best_id, best_edge
435

437	def _emit_doors(plan, rects, walls, tier) -> list[str]:
438	    out: list[str] = []
439	    n = 0
440	    served: set[str] = set()
441	    for adj in plan.adjacency:
442	        if adj.via != "door":
443	            continue
444	        edge = shared_edge(rects[adj.a], rects[adj.b])
445	        partner = adj.a
446	        if edge is None:
447	            # The packer does not guarantee that a room touches the one the plan
448	            # paired it with -- squarify can seat it behind a sibling. Rather
449	            # than leave the room sealed, open it onto whichever neighbour it
450	            # actually shares a wall with. The plan's intent (this room is
451	            # reachable) is honoured even though its literal pairing is not.
452	            partner, edge = _nearest_neighbour(adj.b, rects, exclude={adj.b})
453	        if edge is None:
454	            out.append(f"# TODO_AGENT: room {adj.b} shares no wall long enough for a door "
455	                       f"with any neighbour; it would be sealed")
456	            continue
457	        served.add(adj.b)
458	        served.add(partner)
459	        axis, coord, lo, hi = edge
460	        wall = _wall_for(walls, axis, coord, lo, hi)
461	        if wall is None:
462	            out.append(f"# TODO_AGENT: no wall found between {adj.a} and {adj.b}")
463	            continue
464	        mid = (coord, (lo + hi) / 2.0) if axis == "x" else ((lo + hi) / 2.0, coord)
465	        n += 1
466	        w = door_width(tier, external=False)
467	        tag = f"D-{n:02d}"
468	        note = f"{partner} <-> {adj.b}"
469	        if partner != adj.a:
470	            note += f"  (plan asked for {adj.a}; rerouted to the neighbour it touches)"
471	        out.append(
472	            f"eg.door({tag!r}, on={wall.name!r}, at={snap(_offset_along(wall, mid))}, "
473	            f"width={w}, height=2.05)   # {note}"
474	        )
475	    # An entrance door on the south wall, always -- a house needs a way in.
476	    ext = next((w for w in walls if w.name == "EXT-S"), None)
477	    if ext is not None:
478	        out.append(
479	            f"eg.door('D-00', on='EXT-S', at={snap(ext.length / 2)}, "
480	            f"width={door_width(tier, external=True)}, height=2.10, "
481	            f"external=True, type_name='Eingangstuer')"
482	        )
483	    return out
484	
485	
486	def _emit_windows(plan, rects, walls) -> list[str]:
487	    """Size each habitable room's glazing to satisfy the daylight ratio.
488	
489	    The ratio comes from the plan (BayBO Art. 45 (2) = 1/8), never from a model.
490	    """
491	    from .contracts import HABITABLE
492	    out: list[str] = []
493	    e = plan.envelope
494	    half = e.external_wall_m / 2.0
495	    tol = 0.02
496	    n = 0
497	    for r in plan.rooms:
498	        if r.category not in HABITABLE:
499	            continue
500	        rect = rects[r.id]
501	        sides = []
502	        if abs(rect.y - half) < tol:
503	            sides.append(("EXT-S", rect.w, (rect.x + rect.x2) / 2, rect.y))
504	        if abs(rect.y2 - (e.depth_m - half)) < tol:
505	            sides.append(("EXT-N", rect.w, (rect.x + rect.x2) / 2, rect.y2))
506	        if abs(rect.x - half) < tol:
507	            sides.append(("EXT-W", rect.h, rect.x, (rect.y + rect.y2) / 2))
508	        if abs(rect.x2 - (e.width_m - half)) < tol:
509	            sides.append(("EXT-E", rect.h, rect.x2, (rect.y + rect.y2) / 2))
510	        if not sides:
511	            out.append(f"# TODO_AGENT: room {r.id} ({r.label}) has no exterior wall, "
512	                       f"so it cannot meet the daylight rule; move it to the perimeter")
513	            continue
514	        name, run, cx, cy = max(sides, key=lambda s: s[1])
515	        wall = next((w for w in walls if w.name == name), None)
516	        if wall is None:
517	            continue
518	        need = rect.area * plan.glazing_ratio          # m2 of opening required
519	        height = 1.40
520	        width = min(max(need / height, 0.60), run - 0.60)
521	        if width <= 0.60:
522	            height = 1.80
523	            width = min(max(need / height, 0.60), max(run - 0.60, 0.60))
524	        n += 1
525	        tag = f"F-{n:02d}"
526	        out.append(
527	            f"eg.window({tag!r}, on={name!r}, at={snap(_offset_along(wall, (cx, cy)))}, "
528	            f"width={snap(width)}, height={height}, sill=0.90)   "
529	            f"# {r.id} needs {need:.2f} m2"
530	        )
531	    return out

538	MAX_FIT_ATTEMPTS = 6
539	FIT_STEP = 0.06          # grow the envelope 6% per attempt
540	
541	
542	def fit(plan: ArchitectPlan) -> tuple[ArchitectPlan, dict[str, Rect], int]:
543	    """Lay the plan out, growing the envelope until every room is habitable.
544	
545	    Room areas in an ArchitectPlan are *targets*, and the envelope is the
546	    architect's estimate. When a small room packs into an unusable sliver the
547	    honest response is a slightly larger building, not a 1.05 m wide utility
548	    room -- so the envelope grows by a fixed step and the layout is retried.
549	
550	    Deterministic: same plan in, same envelope out. Returns the adjusted plan,
551	    the footprints, and how many enlargements it took (0 means it fitted as
552	    designed), so the run log can report that the building grew.
553	    """
554	    import copy
555	    for attempt in range(MAX_FIT_ATTEMPTS):
556	        trial = plan if attempt == 0 else copy.deepcopy(plan)
557	        if attempt:
558	            grow = (1.0 + FIT_STEP) ** attempt
559	            trial.envelope.width_m = round(plan.envelope.width_m * grow, 2)
560	            trial.envelope.depth_m = round(plan.envelope.depth_m * grow, 2)
561	        try:
562	            return trial, layout(trial), attempt
563	        except LayoutError as e:
564	            last = e
565	    raise LayoutError(
566	        f"could not fit the programme after {MAX_FIT_ATTEMPTS} enlargements: {last}"
567	    )
568	
569	
570	def translate(plan: ArchitectPlan) -> str:
571	    """The whole L3 step: validated plan in, DSL source out. No tokens spent."""
572	    plan.validate()
573	    fitted, rects, _ = fit(plan)
574	    walls = build_walls(fitted, rects)
575	    return emit(fitted, rects, walls)
576	
577	
578	def translate_to_file(plan: ArchitectPlan, path: str | Path) -> Path:
579	    p = Path(path)
580	    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
581	    p.write_text(translate(plan), encoding="utf-8")
582	    return p

3	    from recognition.design import House

5	    h = House("My house")
6	    eg = h.storey("Erdgeschoss", elevation=0.0, height=2.5)
7	    eg.wall("W1", (0, 0), (12, 0), thickness=0.30, external=True)
8	    eg.room("Küche", [(0.3, 0.3), (4.7, 0.3), (4.7, 4.2), (0.3, 4.2)])
9	    eg.door("D1", on="W1", at=8.3, width=2.01, height=2.2, external=True)
10	    eg.window("F1", on="W1", at=1.5, width=2.0, height=1.2, sill=0.9)
11	    h.write("out/house.ifc")           # 3D: IfcWall / IfcSpace / IfcDoor / IfcWindow with real solids
12	    h.axonometric("out/house.png")     # a quick 3D view
13	    # then: recognition run out/house.ifc out/house   → 2D sheets, schedules, compliance
14	
15	Coordinates are metres in the storey plane (x east, y north); walls are
16	centre-lines; `at` is the distance from the wall's start to the opening's
17	centre. The IFC is deliberately plain — extruded solids, openings cut into
18	walls, standard psets — so any viewer or CAD tool reads it and
19	``recognition.model.load`` gets the same walls, rooms, doors and windows
20	back. Roofs, slabs, stairs and materials are out of scope: this is the layout.

39	@dataclass
40	class Wall:
41	    name: str
42	    start: Pt
43	    end: Pt
44	    thickness: float
45	    height: float
46	    external: bool
47	    entity: ifcopenshell.entity_instance
48	
49	    @property
50	    def length(self) -> float:
51	        return math.dist(self.start, self.end)
52	
53	    @property
54	    def direction(self) -> Pt:
55	        L = self.length
56	        return ((self.end[0] - self.start[0]) / L, (self.end[1] - self.start[1]) / L)
57	
58	    @property
59	    def normal(self) -> Pt:
60	        d = self.direction
61	        return (-d[1], d[0])
62	
63	    def footprint(self, extend: float = 0.0) -> list[Pt]:
64	        d, n, t = self.direction, self.normal, self.thickness / 2
65	        s = (self.start[0] - d[0] * extend, self.start[1] - d[1] * extend)
66	        e = (self.end[0] + d[0] * extend, self.end[1] + d[1] * extend)
67	        return [(s[0] + n[0] * t, s[1] + n[1] * t), (e[0] + n[0] * t, e[1] + n[1] * t),
68	                (e[0] - n[0] * t, e[1] - n[1] * t), (s[0] - n[0] * t, s[1] - n[1] * t)]
69	
70	    def slot(self, at: float, width: float, depth: float) -> list[Pt]:
71	        """Rectangle on the wall axis centred `at` metres from the start, `width` along, `depth` across."""
72	        d, n = self.direction, self.normal
73	        c = (self.start[0] + d[0] * at, self.start[1] + d[1] * at)
74	        w, t = width / 2, depth / 2
75	        return [(c[0] - d[0] * w + n[0] * t, c[1] - d[1] * w + n[1] * t), (c[0] + d[0] * w + n[0] * t, c[1] + d[1] * w + n[1] * t),
76	                (c[0] + d[0] * w - n[0] * t, c[1] + d[1] * w - n[1] * t), (c[0] - d[0] * w - n[0] * t, c[1] - d[1] * w - n[1] * t)]

83	    elevation: float
84	    height: float
85	    entity: ifcopenshell.entity_instance

90	    def wall(self, name: str, start: Pt, end: Pt, thickness: float = 0.30, height: float | None = None,
91	             external: bool = False) -> Wall:
92	        if name in self.walls:
93	            raise ValueError(f"wall {name!r} already exists on {self.name}")
94	        h = height or self.height
95	        ent = self.house._product("IfcWall", name)
96	        wall = Wall(name, tuple(start), tuple(end), thickness, h, external, ent)
97	        self.house._solid(ent, wall.footprint(extend=thickness / 2), self.elevation, h)
98	        run("spatial.assign_container", self.house.f, relating_structure=self.entity, products=[ent])
99	        self.house._pset(ent, "Pset_WallCommon", {"IsExternal": external, "LoadBearing": external})

103	    def room(self, name: str, polygon: list[Pt], height: float | None = None, tag: str | None = None) -> ifcopenshell.entity_instance:
104	        """A room as its floor outline. The name drives the category (Küche → kitchen …)."""
105	        ent = self.house._product("IfcSpace", tag or name)
106	        ent.LongName = name
107	        ent.PredefinedType = "INTERNAL"

114	             external: bool | None = None, type_name: str = "") -> ifcopenshell.entity_instance:
115	        return self._opening("IfcDoor", name, on, at, width, height, sill, external, type_name)

121	    def _opening(self, ifc_class, name, on, at, width, height, sill, external, type_name):
122	        wall = self.walls.get(on)
123	        if wall is None:
124	            raise ValueError(f"no wall {on!r} on {self.name}; have {sorted(self.walls)}")
125	        if not 0 < at < wall.length:

127	        f = self.house.f

130	        self.house._solid(hole, wall.slot(at, width, wall.thickness + 0.04), z, height)
131	        run("feature.add_feature", f, feature=hole, element=wall.entity)
132	        ent = self.house._product(ifc_class, name)
133	        self.house._solid(ent, wall.slot(at, width, max(0.05, wall.thickness / 2)), z, height)

136	            ent.PredefinedType = "DOOR"
137	        run("feature.add_filling", f, opening=hole, element=ent)
138	        run("spatial.assign_container", f, relating_structure=self.entity, products=[ent])
139	        if type_name:

141	            run("type.assign_type", f, related_objects=[ent], relating_type=typ)
142	        self.house._pset(ent, "Pset_DoorCommon" if ifc_class == "IfcDoor" else "Pset_WindowCommon",
143	                         {"IsExternal": wall.external if external is None else external})

187	    def _solid(self, product, polygon: list[Pt], z: float, height: float) -> None:
188	        pts = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in polygon]
189	        if pts[0] != pts[-1]:
190	            pts.append(pts[0])
191	        profile = run("profile.add_arbitrary_profile", self.f, profile=pts, name=product.Name)
192	        rep = run("geometry.add_profile_representation", self.f, context=self.body, profile=profile, depth=float(height))
193	        m = np.eye(4)
194	        m[2, 3] = float(z)
195	        run("geometry.edit_object_placement", self.f, product=product, matrix=m)
196	        run("geometry.assign_representation", self.f, product=product, representation=rep)
